subject: Discovery recap & eval playbook alignment
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Morales <ethan.morales@healthstack.ai>, Sofia Romero <sofia.romero@healthstack.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap & eval playbook alignment

Hi Ethan / Sofia,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Quick recap from our discovery and a proposed path to get an evaluation running that will validate latency, cost, and end-to-end integration for your clinical summarization flow.

High-level takeaways from our call:
- Primary use case: automated clinical note summarization from nightly EHR dumps + clinician-facing editing workflow.
- Main success metrics: 95% gist accuracy (sample-based), average generation latency <1.2s per chunk for interactive edits, and token cost under $0.002/token for bulk nightly runs.
- Data constraints: PHI in EHR; HealthStack prefers VPC/on-prem for evaluation or a redacted-synthetic data path.

Suggested next step: schedule a 60-minute evaluation kickoff (technical deep dive + trial plan alignment). Goals for that session:
1) Align on trial scope and success criteria (we'll draft a mutual action plan).
2) Walk through prompt set and sample outputs; you share a canonical prompt set if available.
3) Confirm environment: Private deployment vs. hosted with contractual controls + data handling.

Can you confirm availability for one of these options (all times PT):
- Tue Dec 8, 11:00am–12:00pm PT
- Wed Dec 9, 9:00am–10:00am PT
- Thu Dec 10, 2:00pm–3:00pm PT

If none work, suggest 2 alternate windows and we’ll loop Kimberly (SE) in for the technical portion. I attached a short playbook and success criteria template to help you fill in details ahead of the call (redwood_trial_playbook.pdf, eval_success_template.docx).

Prep items that would make the session productive:
- A sample of prompts / 10–20 input examples (redacted) — a CSV is fine.
- Clear ownership of what success looks like (a short bulleted list).
- Any compliance constraints (e.g., cannot send PHI to hosted endpoints).

Thanks — I’ll hold the proposed slots until you confirm.

Best,
Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0142
From: Ethan Morales <ethan.morales@healthstack.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Sofia Romero <sofia.romero@healthstack.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:05:12 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap & eval playbook alignment

Ben — thanks for the recap and clear next steps. We’re aligned on the goals you listed.

Availability: week of Dec 7 looks best for us. Our shortlist (PT):
- Tue Dec 8, 11:00am OK for both me and Sofia
- Wed Dec 9, 9:00am is a maybe (Sofia has a conflict)

We’d like Kimberly to lead the technical portion — please loop her in.

Initial success criteria (high level):
- Output accuracy: clinical summaries match physician judgments on 90–95% of sampled cases.
- Latency: interactive edits <1.5s median.
- Integration: API-based ingestion of nightly batches and S3-based output, auth via our Okta tenant.

I’m attaching a first-pass prompt set (healthstack_initial_prompts.csv) with 12 redacted examples. Also flagging that sending PHI to hosted endpoints is not acceptable for our legal team; we’ll need to discuss VPC or an on-prem path during the kickoff.

Thanks — we can confirm Tue Dec 8, 11:00am PT as a tentative hold and finalize when Kimberly confirms.

—Ethan
Ethan Morales
Head of ML Engineering | HealthStack
ethan.morales@healthstack.ai | +1 503-555-0199
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Morales <ethan.morales@healthstack.ai>, Sofia Romero <sofia.romero@healthstack.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 10:22:45 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap & eval playbook alignment

Perfect — thanks for the prompt set, Ethan. Kimberly has availability and will run the technical deep dive. We’ll plan for Tue Dec 8, 11:00am–12:00pm PT as the primary slot and send an invite.

Quick logistics and what we (Redwood) will prepare before the call:
- Kimberly will bring a draft trial plan with a suggested 2-week scoped evaluation (ingest + interactive + batch runs) and a quant plan to measure latency/cost/quality.
- I’ll create a shared Drive folder with the playbook and a short questionnaire for legal/compliance so you can flag redaction requirements.
- We can demo both Hosted with strict contract controls and Redwood Private (VPC) flow; decision on the deployment mode can happen after the first technical run.

I attached an .ics stub (invite.ics) and a one-page playbook we’ll iterate on. Also adding our HubSpot deal link for reference: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/HS-2026-0123.

If you have an internal calendar link you prefer, send it over and we’ll use that instead.

See you on the 8th — Kimberly, want to add anything?

Thanks,
Ben
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Morales <ethan.morales@healthstack.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 08:15:30 -0800
Subject: Technical prep: Dec 8 eval kickoff

Ethan — looking forward to the session. A few technical asks so we can make the hour productive:

Pre-call items (please share if possible):
- A few representative EHR notes (redacted) or synthetic equivalents — 10–20 files.
- Your preferred auth flow (Okta OIDC details) and sample S3 write permissions for output bucket.
- Any specific model constraints (e.g., prefer 4k context models, quantization requirements).

Draft agenda for the 60-minute session:
1) 0–10 min: Introductions and success criteria quick-check (Ben)
2) 10–30 min: Architecture and data flow (Kimberly)
3) 30–45 min: Prompt walkthrough and sample outputs (live)
4) 45–55 min: Trial plan / metrics and measurement (Lauren joins for ops)
5) 55–60 min: Next steps and mutual action items

I’m attaching a slightly updated trial playbook (trial_playbook_v2.pdf) with more specifics on measurement and sample prompts. If you can drop the CSV into the shared folder I’ll pre-run a few locally (on synthetic data) and bring example outputs.

If any of the above is a blocker (e.g., cannot share files at all), tell me and we’ll propose a redaction/synthetic path to validate prompts and latency without PHI.

Cheers,
Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com
From: Ethan Morales <ethan.morales@healthstack.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Technical prep: Dec 8 eval kickoff

Thanks — confirmed for Tue Dec 8, 11:00am–12:00pm PT. I’ve accepted the calendar hold (we used the invite.ics).

I uploaded the CSV you referenced to S3 (pre-authenticated link in our shared folder) and attached a short final list of success criteria inline:
- Clinical fidelity: physician-reviewed summaries accurate on >=92% of cases in a 50-sample spot check.
- Latency: median interactive response <1.3s, p95 <2.2s.
- Cost: projected nightly run at scale <= $1,200 for our expected token volumes.

We cannot send raw PHI to hosted endpoints — legal will only sign off on a Private deployment or a redaction/synthetic evaluation. We’ll share Okta OIDC details during the kickoff.

Attached: healthstack_initial_prompts.csv (already uploaded), final_success_criteria.txt (short list).

Looking forward to it.

—Ethan
